title: You're braking
in a straight line.
That's why you're slow.
slides.sub: Trail braking, explained in 8 slides. ~~Save it for your next session.~~

title: Release the brake
as you turn in.
slides.body: Hit peak pressure in a straight line, then **bleed it off as you add steering**. You're fully off the brake around the apex, ~~not at the turn-in point.~~

title: Braking loads
the front tyres.
slides.body: Braking shifts weight forward. A loaded front tyre has more grip, so the car **turns in sharper**. Release too early and that grip leaves with it.

title: Thick line =
more brake.
slides.body: Peak pressure on the straight, a **steady taper** from turn-in to the apex. Brake and steering overlap. That overlap is the trail.
slides.note: Corner sketch · not a real track

before.label: Before · snap release
before.body: The front unloads right at turn-in. ~~Understeer, a late apex, a slow exit.~~

after.label: After · smooth taper
after.body: The front stays loaded while you steer. **The car rotates**, so you can get back on the throttle sooner.

title: Read the
symptom.

rows: Released too early or too fast
Too much pressure with lock on
Release more as steering goes in
Too much brake and steering together

slides.note: General guide · every car is different

steps.title: Pick one slow corner
steps.body: A hairpin or a tight 90° is easiest to feel.

steps.title: Brake at your usual marker
steps.body: Same point every lap. Change one thing at a time.

steps.title: Bleed the pressure off as you steer
steps.body: Aim to reach zero around the apex.

steps.title: Watch your brake trace
steps.body: If your sim shows inputs: **a ramp, not a cliff**.

title: Smooth in.
Fast out.
slides.body: Trail braking is the biggest single jump in pace for most sim racers I coach. **Try the drill tonight**, then tell me which corner you picked.
